newsitem.title: UK: Agents probe HK's last governor Patten - report.
newsitem.headline: Agents probe HK's last governor Patten - report.

text.p: Hong Kong's last Governor Chris Patten is being investigated by British MI6 intelligence officers and could be prosecuted for allegedly leaking secret documents, The Sunday Times said.

The paper said Foreign Office officials are pressing for Patten to be prosecuted under Britain's Offical Secrets Act for allegedly leaking to writer and broadcaster Jonathan Dimbleby details of a secret deal with China over Hong Kong's future.
The colony was handed back to China at the end of June after 156 years of British colonial rule.
A Foreign Office spokesman refused to comment on the front-page newspaper report and Dimbleby said he never divulged information about his sources.
The Sunday Times said the row was sparked by its publication of extracts from Dimbleby's forthcoming book on Governor Patten's last days in office.
Patten was said to have been angry at Britain's failure to bring in direct elections in Hong Kong from 1988 in order to hand over a democratic administration to China.
He is said to have claimed that Britain gave in to China.
